PullRequest.Title: agentHost: reduce artifact tool overhead with a prompt experiment
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Add the experiment-configurable `chat.artifactTools.compactPrompts` setting, defaulting to **false** (verbose/control). The treatment key is `config.chat.artifactTools.compactPrompts`. Compact prompts reduce repeated classification prose and first-turn guidance while retaining the full eligibility contract in the Add tool description for restored chats.
- Keep List/Remove deferral **independent of the prompt experiment**. Typed per-tool metadata keeps Add eager, uses Copilot discovery when its existing search gate is active, and uses Claude's native MCP loading metadata. Codex stays eager because the host cannot reliably determine native search support.
- Make Add idempotently promote references in place, preserve IDs and atomic batches, and return concise per-item mutation results. Preserve actual tool names, legacy aliases, feature gating, explicit removal, and user-visible labels. The existing authoritative PR-creation registration path remains unchanged.

## Experiment and measurement

Start a new chat after changing the prompt setting. Both variants use the same deferral behavior and shared eligibility/discovery clarifications; the control retains the original verbose format rather than reproducing the old payload byte-for-byte.

Local `o200k_base` measurements of serialized tool-definition arrays plus the first-turn reminder, with List/Remove deferred in both variants:

| Artifact-specific payload | Control | Compact |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial tool definitions | 568 | 500 |
| First-turn reminder | 218 | 46 |
| Total | 786 | 546 |

This is **240 fewer initial artifact-specific tokens** from prompt compaction. The eager fallback also saves 240 tokens (888 to 648). Measurements exclude provider framing and later discovery overhead and do **not** establish total-session cost or AIU savings.

## Validation

- 83 targeted Electron tests and 8 Node checks passed, including native Claude SDK/MCP invocation.
- Coverage includes experiment defaults/overrides and host sync, both prompt variants, discovery and invocation, restored/legacy compatibility, gate off/on, first-turn reminders, multi-item adds, duplicate/promotion behavior, atomic failures, URI validation, persistence, and removal.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, changed-file ESLint, `npm run gulp compile-client`, `npm run precommit` (23 staged files), and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full Copilot E2E replay could not complete: the standalone agent host timed out during startup before the scenario ran. No replay recordings were changed; the existing batch-result assertion was updated for the compact success response.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: All server-tool descriptions and schemas were forced eager on each Copilot session launch/resume, so rarely used artifact List/Remove metadata consumed prompt serialization and model-context tokens even when never invoked.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Unnecessary initial prompt bytes/tokens on artifact-enabled Copilot sessions, increasing request payload and model-context overhead.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Artifact List and Remove metadata is excluded from the eager Copilot tool set when tool search is available and loaded through the existing search mechanism only when needed; Add remains eager and unsupported models retain the previous fallback.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, CopilotAgentSession._createServerSdkTools mapped every enabled server tool to `defer: 'never'`; CopilotSessionLauncher calls createServerSdkTools on each launch/resume and includes those definitions in the SDK tool array. Artifact list/remove definitions are only needed when those uncommon operations are requested, yet were therefore loaded into every artifact-enabled Copilot model context. The changed line now maps definitions marked deferLoading to `defer: 'auto'` when the already-established tool-search gate is active, while artifactServerTools marks only List/Remove deferred and leaves Add eager. Tests trace discovery through the existing tool-search client round-trip in both new and restored chats.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or resume an artifact-enabled Copilot, Claude, or Codex chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider materialization builds the session tool definitions before the chat can use the model. Copilot passes SDK tools at launch/resume; Claude builds an in-process MCP server before startup wiring completes; Codex includes dynamicTools in the thread/start JSON-RPC request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send model/tool definitions through the provider SDK as part of session startup and subsequent model use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A constant three artifact tools per artifact-enabled session; after the diff, Copilot with active tool search and Claude eagerly load only Add while List/Remove remain discoverable. Codex keeps all three eager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All three artifact tools were eager for Copilot and Claude; Codex remains eager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tool wiring must complete before the provider session starts; reducing eager definitions lowers initial prompt/model-context payload. No unbounded user collection is serialized here.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send Codex thread/start with dynamicTools to the Codex process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One JSON-RPC request per thread start containing the same three artifact tools when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three artifact definitions were sent eagerly at thread/start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is on Codex chat startup, but the diff intentionally strips/ignores deferral metadata and does not increase tool cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of concurrent chat materializations; artifact-tool cardinality is fixed at three per session rather than scaling with workspace or artifact count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One materialization pipeline per chat. Claude creates its constant-size tool wrappers with Promise.all; Copilot and Codex map them synchronously. There is no collection-driven concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Definitions and schemas are module-level immutable arrays; prompt selection reads current in-memory root configuration when materializing. There is no miss cache or repeated expensive recomputation. Restored sessions refresh metadata by name but retain materialized membership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider call paths and constant cardinality are directly traced. The removed eager prompt cost is concrete; exact latency/token savings vary by provider framing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact network-token and startup-latency savings depend on provider serialization and model. Codex receives no deferral benefit, but its payload remains constant-size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff removes eager List/Remove metadata where supported and preserves an eager fallback where discovery support is unknown. This is recorded as a regression fix for Copilot's prior forced-eager path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first turn in a fresh or empty restored chat with artifact tools enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ArtifactToolsContribution contributes one instruction before the first outgoing model turn; its chat memento suppresses the instruction on later turns and on restored chats that already contain turns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Include the selected artifact instruction in the outgoing model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly once per fresh chat, including an empty restored chat; zero on subsequent turns and non-empty restored histories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One verbose artifact instruction was included on the first outgoing turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The instruction is part of the model request. Compact treatment reduces bytes; control remains verbose and adds only constant wording.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of newly created chats, not turn count or history length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous configuration read and one string selection per chat's first turn; no parallel work or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A per-chat memento is the coalescing state: cold empty chats receive guidance once; warm chats do not. The treatment value is read from in-memory synchronized configuration, with no external lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the memento gate and tests for fresh, restored, and second-turn behavior directly establish frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider tokenization determines exact savings; the default control's small wording growth is bounded and not a meaningful regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Work remains once-per-chat and constant-size; compact mode reduces prompt serialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: List or remove an artifact after List/Remove tools are deferred
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On Copilot with active tool search, the model invokes tool_search, the host emits a client action and waits for session/toolCallComplete, then returns references to both deferred artifact tools; the selected server tool then executes in process. Claude uses SDK-native MCP discovery. Codex remains direct/eager.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Round-trip Copilot tool-search candidates to the workbench client and await session/toolCallComplete.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery call when the model needs either deferred operation; one result can expose both artifact tools. It does not scale with artifact count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: List and Remove were eager and could be invoked without this discovery round-trip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly on the critical path for a requested List/Remove operation when Copilot search is active, trading rare-operation latency for lower prompt cost on every session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Claude SDK-native lazy MCP tool discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two of the three artifact tools are marked not-always-loaded in one per-session MCP server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The SDK received no alwaysLoad override, so all artifact tools followed its previous default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider-native discovery may precede first List/Remove use; Add remains immediately available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats that actually request list/remove, with fixed candidate cardinality two after effective grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single search invocation can return both List and Remove. Copilot pending calls are keyed by tool-call id; no new fan-out occurs. The provider controls whether later turns reuse discovered references.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The host has no separate discovery cache; Copilot returns toolReferences through the SDK's existing deferred-tool mechanism and Claude delegates lifecycle to the native SDK. Add is never deferred; unsupported Copilot models and Codex retain eager behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added Copilot client round-trip and fixed candidate count; medium for Claude's internal latency because SDK-native discovery details are outside the repository.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: List/remove prevalence and provider reuse across turns are not established. Their uncommon administrative nature and the intentional global prompt reduction make the bounded extra discovery latency non-reportable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The latency tradeoff is explicit, bounded to two rare tools, preserves an eager fallback, and avoids per-artifact or per-session-history fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add or promote a batch of artifacts and persist session state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Add tool validates all inputs, serializes mutations per session, updates the immutable collection, performs one awaited catalog persistence when state changed, then publishes session metadata and returns compact IDs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize updated session artifact metadata with the session catalog/database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero writes for an unchanged duplicate-only batch; exactly one awaited write for any mutating batch, regardless of item count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A mutating batch likewise performed one persistence operation through SessionArtifacts.mutate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Durable persistence remains on the Add/Remove critical path and must finish before state publication and tool completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: For m batch inputs and n existing artifacts, immutable find/copy processing remains roughly O(m*n + m^2); a reference-to-artifact promotion adds one O(n) map for that promoted entry. Expected artifact batches are small and the prior add loop already had the same dominant scan/copy scaling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SequencerByKey serializes mutations for the same session while allowing different sessions independently. A batch is processed synchronously and persisted once; no Promise.all boundary burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current artifacts are read from in-memory session state for each queued mutation. Duplicate detection uses the current immutable collection; there is no separate index or negative cache. Unchanged duplicates retain array identity and skip persistence.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: mutation, sequencing, identity-based write suppression, and persistence call paths are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No repository evidence shows realistically large artifact batches or lists. The extra promotion map occurs only for reference-to-artifact transitions and does not justify a performance finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Persistence remains coalesced to one write per mutating batch, same-session ordering is preserved, and the added promotion work is bounded to an uncommon transition.

Scenarios.Scenario: Synchronize the compact-prompt experiment setting into the agent host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration registration adds one application-scoped boolean to the existing host synchronization patch; the agent host reads the synchronized root value during prompt/tool materialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward root configuration from the renderer/host starter to local or remote agent hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional boolean in each existing configuration synchronization payload for local, remote-extension-host, or remote targets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing artifact-enabled setting was synchronized; the compact-prompt boolean was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant-size payload addition during existing host configuration synchronization; no separate IPC call is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one boolean per synchronization payload, independent of sessions, workspace size, or artifacts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing configuration synchronization controls transport and ordering; this change adds one scalar field and no new task, listener, or parallel request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The root configuration is retained by AgentConfigurationService and read synchronously; no repeated filesystem/network reads or cache invalidation loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration metadata and synchronization tests establish transport behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the byte increase is constant and negligible.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 24 changed files and every diff page. No actionable diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold. The change primarily reduces eager prompt/tool metadata, preserves constant-size provider setup and one-write batch persistence, and introduces only a bounded intentional discovery round-trip for rare List/Remove operations. One concrete prior forced-eager Copilot regression fix was recorded for internal learning.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
